# Fork-local file inventory for v2 porting

**Status:** **frozen — migration declared complete 2026-05-22** (see [p3-notes.md §22](p3-notes.md)). **Last updated:** 2026-05-22. **Generated by:** P0 / W0.5. **Source HEAD:** `85a39ae0e8c4f6e103cecf325d8c444bda7109e6` (branch `main`, v1.2.71).

> 🏁 **All P4 + P5 items have a final disposition.** Items still labelled `port` that did not actually ship on v2 by the closure date are now `deferred` — see the disposition column for each, and §22.2 of `p3-notes.md` for the operator-facing summary of what's deferred and why. If a deferred item gets ported later, edit the row in place + add a new `## §N` entry to `p3-notes.md`.

**Index source:** [`../fork-divergence.md`](../fork-divergence.md). **Disposition source:** [`../archive/v2-motivation-and-context.md`](../archive/v2-motivation-and-context.md) §6 (archived). **Phase mapping source:** [`../archive/v2-implementation-plan.md`](../archive/v2-implementation-plan.md) §5 (archived).

This is the P4/P5 porting checklist. Every fork-local code surface that needs a decision at migration time must appear here. If a file isn't here, it's either (a) upstream-derived code that will be wholesale replaced by v2 (e.g. `src/db.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/message-loop.ts`) and needs no port, or (b) a gap — flag it and update this document.

LOC values are `wc -l` at HEAD and will drift; treat them as 2026-05-21 snapshots.

## Disposition legend

- **port** — re-apply the fork code on top of v2's host shape; v2 has no equivalent or the v2 equivalent is insufficient.
- **port-customizations-only** — v2 has the file (e.g. via skill install) but our fork has substantive deltas; re-apply the deltas only.
- **retire-replaced-by-v2** — v2 ships an equivalent module that covers our use case; drop our code.
- **retire-replaced-by-skill** — v2 distributes equivalent functionality as an upstream skill; apply the skill instead.
- **resolved** — already handled by a planned P2 step (e.g. credential proxy via W2.4).
- **decide-at-port-time** — disposition depends on what v2's equivalent module actually covers; pick one of the above during the work unit.
- **modify-upstream-file** — fork's contribution is a small patch on a file that exists upstream; surgically re-apply rather than porting a whole file.
- **deferred** — recognised at closure (2026-05-22) but intentionally not ported; reopen on demand. See `p3-notes.md` §22.2.

## P4 — Journal MCP integration (modifies upstream files)

The Journal MCP integration is two surgical patches across two files, not a standalone module. Both must be re-applied in W4.7. Bun-runtime quirks (`bun:sqlite` parameter syntax) only matter if the integration touches DB code; current implementation is HTTP-only, so the risk is mostly env-var pass-through and SDK options shape on v2's Bun container.

| Site | Lines | What it does | P4 unit | Disposition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container/agent-runner/src/index.ts` | 410–417 | Conditional `journal` MCP server in the SDK `mcpServers` block when `JOURNAL_MCP_URL` is set; adds `Authorization: Bearer` header if `JOURNAL_API_TOKEN` is set. | W4.7 | **superseded 2026-05-22** — v2 replaces the env-var-conditional registration with per-group `container.json` `mcpServers` map. Main group already wired (`groups/main/container.json` → `type: http`, `url: http://192.168.2.105:8400/mcp`, bearer auth). See [p3-notes.md §19](p3-notes.md). |
| `src/container-runner.ts` | 314–330 | Pass-through of `JOURNAL_MCP_URL` and `JOURNAL_API_TOKEN` from host env to the container via `-e` flags. | W4.7 | **superseded 2026-05-22** — no env pass-through needed; MCP config is read from per-group `container.json`. |

## Items the planning session missed

Flagged here so they land somewhere durable rather than getting re-discovered mid-port:

1. **`src/transcription.ts` (142 LOC)** — fork-local OpenAI Whisper integration not listed in `docs/fork-divergence.md` or motivation-and-context.md §6. Disposition: retire-replaced-by-skill via `/add-voice-transcription`. Recommend back-porting an entry into `docs/fork-divergence.md` post-cutover.

2. **`src/whatsapp-auth.ts` (180 LOC)** — referenced in `docs/fork-divergence.md` § "WhatsApp Bundled in Core" but absent from the W0.5 auto-scan file list. Logically part of W5.2 (the WhatsApp channel port).

3. **`container/agent-runner/src/index.ts:410-417` + `src/container-runner.ts:314-330`** — Journal MCP integration is *two code sites in upstream-derived files*, not a standalone fork-local file. The W0.5 auto-scan file list (`for f in src/credential-proxy.ts ...`) cannot capture this shape. W4.7 handles it but the inventory has to call it out explicitly.

4. **Telegram channel (`src/channels/telegram.ts`, 299 LOC)** — bundled in this fork's `main` but not in production. Plan's W5 only covers Slack/WA/Gmail. Confirmed disposition: do not port; not used.

5. **WA Baileys keystore (`store/auth-personal-backup/*`)** — 470 backup entries in the W0.3 tarball. Migration by `migrate-v2.sh` per W3.4 is the assumed path; if that path doesn't cover the keystore, W5.2 needs a manual copy step. Flag and verify in W3.4.

## Total porting surface

- **Host code (P4):** ~2,000 LOC across 10 files, of which ~125 LOC (`credential-proxy.ts`) is **retired** post-P1 (OneCLI handles subscription auth natively — see [spike-notes.md](spike-notes.md) §3).
- **Channels (P5):** ~1,700 LOC of fork customizations across slack/whatsapp/gmail (telegram excluded).
- **Surgical patches:** Journal MCP integration (≈25 lines spread across 2 files).
- **Total active porting work for P4+P5:** ~3,575 LOC of fork code (~3,700 minus the 125 LOC retired credential-proxy), of which a further portion (status-tracker, mount-security, sender-allowlist, /status, transcription) is likely retirable in favour of v2 equivalents.
